chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The sneezing is a good thing; it benefits the body and reminds [one] of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' I said, 'Among us there is a group of people who say,
He (peace be upon him) said: 'If they are lying, may they not attain the intercession of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical significance of sneezing in Shia hadith, and what is the consequence for those who deny the Prophet's share in it?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) highlights sneezing as both a physical benefit and a spiritual reminder of Allah, countering skeptics who deny the Prophet's specific connection to this act by asserting that their denial would forfeit their share in his intercession. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on the Prophet's comprehensive role in daily acts of worship, linking bodily functions to divine remembrance. The reference to intercession (Shafa'ah) serves as a theological guarantee of the truth of the Prophet's teachings against those who dismiss them.
